pages.title: Velocity Verlet
pages.summary: Positions and velocities advance together with half-step kicks around a full drift. The scheme is time-reversible and symplectic, so the energy of an unthermostatted run fluctuates without drifting when the time step is small enough.
pages.equation: v(t+½Δt) = v(t) + ½Δt F(t)/m;  x(t+Δt) = x(t) + Δt v(t+½Δt);  v(t+Δt) = v(t+½Δt) + ½Δt F(t+Δt)/m
symbols: Field, else GAFF (C, H) or UFF
from the element or the data file
pages.when: Every molecular-dynamics run in CAPS. All-atom models with hydrogens need Δt ≤ 1 fs: CAPS has no bond constraints (SHAKE, LINCS) yet.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Stochastic velocity rescaling (CSVR)
pages.summary: CSVR rescales all velocities by one factor each step. The factor is drawn so that the kinetic energy follows the stochastic equation below, which samples the canonical ensemble exactly while disturbing the dynamics as little as a Berendsen thermostat does. CAPS draws the new kinetic energy in one step from its exact distribution, as in the paper's appendix.
pages.equation: dK = (K̄ − K) dt/τ + 2 √(K K̄ / N_f) dW / √τ
symbols: target kinetic energy, N_f k_B T / 2
degrees of freedom: 3N − 3, held atoms excluded
Wiener noise: one Gaussian and a χ² sum of N_f − 1 per step
mt19937-64 stream from the run's seed
pages.when: The default for NVT and NPT in CAPS. The energy it exchanges with the bath is tracked, so the conserved quantity reports integration error. Prefer Langevin (BAOAB) for far-from-equilibrium starts that need strong damping.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Langevin dynamics (BAOAB)
pages.summary: Each step splits into half kicks (B), half drifts (A) and an exact Ornstein–Uhlenbeck update of the velocities (O) in the order B A O A B. The splitting gives accurate configurational averages at larger friction than other Langevin schemes.
pages.equation: O:  v ← c₁ v + c₂ √(k_B T / m) ξ,   c₁ = exp(−γ Δt),   c₂ = √(1 − c₁²)
symbols: mt19937-64 stream from the run's seed
pages.when: Robust thermalisation of stiff or strained starts. The friction slows diffusion and relaxation, so measure dynamics (MSD, relaxation times) with CSVR instead.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Nosé–Hoover chains and MTK pressure coupling
pages.summary: A chain of three thermostat variables couples to the particles' kinetic energy, each link thermostatting the one before; the equations are deterministic and time-reversible, and the extended system's energy is conserved. For constant pressure the logarithm of the volume becomes a dynamical variable with its own mass and chain (Martyna–Tobias–Klein), driven by the difference between the instantaneous and target pressure. CAPS integrates both exactly as LAMMPS's fix nvt and fix npt iso do: chain half-steps (Trotter splitting) around velocity Verlet, the cell scaled in two half-steps around the drift.
pages.equation: ṗ_i = F_i − (η̇₁ + (1 + 3/N_f) ε̇) p_i,   Q₁ η̈₁ = Σ p²/m − N_f k_B T − Q₁ η̇₁ η̇₂,   W ε̈ = 3V (P − P₀) + (3/N_f) Σ p²/m − W ε̇ η̇ₚ₁
pages.equation_note: Martyna, Klein & Tuckerman 1992; Martyna, Tobias & Klein 1994
symbols: N_f k_B T τ_T², k_B T τ_T² (τ_T the damping time)
pages.when: Production NVT and NPT runs that must match LAMMPS (or GROMACS Nose-Hoover/MTTK) exactly; for equilibration from a poor start the Bussi thermostat and stochastic cell rescaling relax faster.
pages.tested: Dynamics.NoseHooverChainsAndMtkBarostat · scripts/check_lammps.sh (fix nvt, fix npt iso: positions within 1.5e-5 Å after 400 steps)
pages.deviation: isotropic pressure coupling only; not with bond constraints or r-RESPA

pages.title: Berendsen pressure coupling
pages.summary: The cell and all positions are scaled so that the pressure relaxes exponentially towards the target. It controls the density quickly but does not sample the isothermal–isobaric ensemble: volume fluctuations are too small.
pages.equation: μ = exp(−β Δt_p (P₀ − P) / (3 τ_P)),   x ← μ x,   h ← μ h
pages.equation_note: Berendsen et al. 1984, in CAPS's exponential form
pages.when: Early equilibration and the lateral axes of a tensile test (per-axis form). Use stochastic cell rescaling for production NPT.
pages.deviation: exponential rather than linear scaling; the volume change is limited to 1 % per update; a per-axis variant scales each axis from P_kk

pages.title: Stochastic cell rescaling
pages.summary: A first-order barostat like Berendsen's, with a noise term that restores the correct volume fluctuations of the isothermal–isobaric ensemble. Velocities are scaled by the inverse factor so the kinetic energy stays consistent.
pages.equation: dε = −(β/τ_P)(P₀ − P) dt + √(2 k_B T β dt / (V τ_P)) dW,   μ = exp(dε/3),   v ← v/μ
symbols: compressibility (sets the response, not the result)
mt19937-64 stream from the run's seed
pages.when: The default barostat for NPT production and for the NPT stages of equilibration protocols.
pages.deviation: the −k_B T/V term of the drift is left out (a fraction of an atmosphere for cells of thousands of atoms); isotropic only; dε limited to ±1 % per update

pages.title: Damped shifted force (DSF)
pages.summary: A pairwise alternative to Ewald sums: the Coulomb interaction is damped by erfc and shifted so that both the energy and the force go to zero at the cut-off. It converges to Ewald results for condensed phases at modest cost.
pages.equation: E = q_i q_j [ erfc(αr)/r − erfc(αr_c)/r_c + (erfc(αr_c)/r_c² + (2α/√π) exp(−α²r_c²)/r_c)(r − r_c) ],  r < r_c
symbols: cut-off, shared with van der Waals
pages.when: The default electrostatics in CAPS: cheap, no grid, fine for neutral bulk polymers. Use smooth PME for ionic systems, interfaces with net dipoles, or when comparing with Ewald-based codes.
pages.deviation: bonded partners are treated as LAMMPS coul/dsf does (the damped sum includes them, the excluded part is removed)

pages.title: Smooth particle-mesh Ewald (SPME)
pages.summary: The Ewald sum split into a short-ranged real-space part and a smooth reciprocal part evaluated on a grid: charges are spread with B-splines, transformed by FFT, multiplied by the influence function and gathered back as forces.
pages.equation: E_rec = (1/2πV) Σ_{m≠0} exp(−π²m²/β²)/m² · B(m) |F(Q)(m)|²,   erfc(β r_c) = ε_rel
pages.when: Charged or strongly polar systems, ionic crystals, interfaces, and whenever results must match Ewald-based codes. Periodic cells only; about 1.5 × the cost of DSF in MD.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Ewald summation (reference)
pages.summary: The plain Ewald sum over reciprocal-lattice vectors. CAPS keeps it as the reference the PME kernel is tested against; runs use PME.
pages.equation: E = E_real + E_rec + E_self,   E_self = −(β/√π) Σ q_i²
symbols: enough for 10⁻⁸ relative accuracy in tests
pages.when: Not offered for runs: its cost grows as N^{3/2}–N². It checks PME forces, energy and virial.
pages.deviation: reference only

pages.title: L-BFGS
pages.summary: A quasi-Newton minimiser that approximates the inverse Hessian from the last few steps (two-loop recursion). It is the fastest of CAPS's minimisers for smooth energies of thousands of atoms.
pages.equation: d = −H_k ∇E,  H_k from the last m pairs (s_i = x_{i+1} − x_i, y_i = ∇E_{i+1} − ∇E_i)
symbols: stop when the largest atomic force is below
or the relative energy change is below
pages.when: The default minimiser. After growth with a contact scale below 1, run the capped push-off first (Relax does by default).
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: FIRE
pages.summary: A damped dynamics minimiser: velocities are mixed towards the force direction and the time step grows while the power F·v stays positive; the motion stops when it turns uphill.
pages.equation: v ← (1 − α) v + α |v| F/|F|,  if F·v < 0: v = 0, Δt ← Δt f_dec, α = α_start
pages.when: Rough starts with large forces, where line searches struggle.
pages.deviation: standard parameters of the paper

pages.title: Conjugate gradients and steepest descent
pages.summary: Steepest descent follows the force; Polak–Ribière conjugate gradients mixes in the previous direction so successive steps do not undo each other.
symbols: Polak–Ribière coefficient, reset to 0 when negative
pages.when: Comparison and teaching; L-BFGS is faster for the same tolerance.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Capped-force push-off
pages.summary: Overlapping atoms (from growth with lowered contact limits, or packing) make Lennard-Jones forces explode. The push-off caps them: inside the radius where the force would exceed the cap the potential becomes linear, and the cap is raised stage by stage while minimising. Optionally the push-off runs first as NVT dynamics, as in the paper: the cap is raised geometrically over a set time (the λ ramp) so chains move apart by motion before the minimisation stages.
pages.equation: F_LJ(r) → sign(F) · min(|F_LJ(r)|, F_cap),   F_cap = 5, 20, 100 … F_final kcal/mol/Å;   MD: F_cap,k = 5 (F_final/5)^(k/9), k = 0 … 9, each for t_ramp/10
symbols: 5, 20, 100, then the chosen final cap (500 by default)
λ ramp: the time of the MD push-off
20 ps on the Relax board; 0 = minimisation stages only
NVT temperature of the MD push-off (Bussi thermostat, 1 fs)
pages.when: Always before minimising a grown or packed cell; Relax does it by default.
pages.deviation: the cap is raised in ten NVT segments rather than continuously; Coulomb terms are off during the push-off

pages.title: Chain growth by trial placement
pages.summary: Chains grow unit by unit inside the periodic cell. Each step places the next backbone atom and its substituents from internal coordinates (NeRF), tries many torsions (trans and gauche with jitter, ring rotations) and keeps the roomiest: the trial whose worst distance to any atom already in the cell, minus its contact limit, is largest. A poor step backs up a few units; a chain that cannot continue restarts elsewhere.
pages.equation: keep argmax_trials  min_j ( |r − r_j| − ℓ(z, z_j) · s )
symbols: 1, or lowered step by step when crowded (then push-off)
pages.when: Building amorphous cells, films on surfaces and blends at a chosen density. Measure chain dimensions only after equilibration.
pages.deviation: not configurational-bias Monte Carlo: trials are ranked by geometric room, not Boltzmann weights, so the grown chains are not a Rosenbluth-weighted ensemble

pages.title: Overlap-penalty packing
pages.summary: Molecules are rigid bodies (centre and rotation). A smooth penalty for atoms of different molecules closer than the tolerance, plus penalties for leaving their regions, is minimised with L-BFGS; the worst-placed molecules are moved between rounds.
pages.equation: f = Σ_{i<j, different molecules} max(0, d² − |x_i − x_j|²)² + w Σ_i g_region(x_i)²
pages.when: Solvents, fluids in pores, curatives inserted into a cell, mixtures from packmol input files.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Universal force field (UFF)
pages.summary: Every element from H to Lr, typed from its bonds, hybridisation and oxidation state. Used for clean-up and for any structure the other force fields cannot type (metals, silicon, phosphorus, halogens).
pages.equation: E = Σ k(r − r₀)² + Σ K[C₀ + C₁ cos θ + C₂ cos 2θ] + Σ ½V[1 − cos(nφ₀) cos(nφ)] + Σ D[(x/r)¹² − 2(x/r)⁶] + inversions
symbols: natural bond length r_i + r_j + r_BO − r_EN
van der Waals well and distance
pages.when: Geometry clean-up of any molecule; runs on structures outside GAFF's scope. UFF has no charges of its own: use QEq when electrostatics matter.
pages.deviation: functional forms and special cases follow RDKit's UFF, whose parameter table CAPS carries; LAMMPS export checked term by term

pages.title: Charge equilibration (QEq)
pages.summary: Charges that equalise the electronegativity of every atom at fixed total charge, for any element. The energy below is minimised; the linear system is solved by conjugate gradients.
pages.equation: E(q) = Σ χ_i q_i + ½ Σ J_i q_i² + Σ_{i<j} q_i q_j K(r_ij),   K = 14.40 / √(r² + a_ij²) eV,   a_ij = 7.20 (1/J_i + 1/J_j) Å
pages.equation_note: Rappé & Goddard 1991, with the Ohno–Klopman kernel
symbols: Ohno–Klopman, tapered to zero at the cut-off
pages.when: Charges for structures with metals, silicon or other elements without force-field charges, such as fillers and coupling agents. Like the original QEq it gives ionic crystals large charges (quartz O ≈ −1.6 e).
pages.deviation: the Ohno–Klopman kernel with a 7th-order taper replaces the paper's Slater-orbital Coulomb integrals; J of hydrogen does not depend on its charge

pages.title: General AMBER force field (GAFF)
pages.summary: Atom types for organic molecules assigned by rules in antechamber's order (rings, aromaticity, conjugation), with AMBER functional forms: harmonic bonds and angles, cosine torsions, 12–6 Lennard-Jones, 1–4 interactions scaled by ½ (LJ) and 1/1.2 (Coulomb).
pages.equation: E = Σ k_b(r − r₀)² + Σ k_θ(θ − θ₀)² + Σ (V_n/2)[1 + cos(nφ − γ)] + Σ 4ε[(σ/r)¹² − (σ/r)⁶] + Σ q_i q_j / r
symbols: c3, ca, hc, ha … assigned by rules
pages.when: Organic polymers and additives. CAPS's built-in default for pure hydrocarbons; the library also holds GAFF2 and the other published force fields, with CAPS typing rules.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Gasteiger–Marsili charges (PEOE)
pages.summary: Partial equalisation of orbital electronegativity: charge flows along each bond from the less to the more electronegative atom, in six iterations damped by half each time, so it stays local.
pages.equation: χ_i = a_i + b_i q_i + c_i q_i²,   Δq_i = Σ_j (χ_j − χ_i)/χ⁺ · ½ᵏ
symbols: H, C, N, O (sp³, sp², sp), F, Cl, Br, I, sp³ S
pages.when: Quick charges for organic molecules. Other elements are refused; use QEq for them.
pages.deviation: parameters of Table 1 plus the sp³ sulfur extension

pages.title: 21-step compression and decompression
pages.summary: Alternating NVT heating, NVT cooling and NPT compression up to a maximum pressure, then decompression stages, then a final NPT stage at the target conditions. It relaxes the density of glassy polymer cells far faster than plain NPT at room temperature.
pages.equation: 21 stages: heat T_max / cool T_final / compress 0.02, 0.6, 1.0 P_max …, decompress 0.5, 0.1, 0.01 P_max, final NPT at P_final
pages.when: Glassy polymer cells before property calculations. Rubbers far above Tg equilibrate with plain NPT.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Structure factors: S(q), X-ray and neutron
pages.summary: At low q the exact sum over every reciprocal-lattice vector the cell allows; above the switch-over, the Fourier transform of the partial pair distributions with a Lorch window against truncation ripples. X-ray and neutron patterns weight the partials by form factors or scattering lengths (Faber–Ziman).
pages.equation: S(q) = 1 + (|Σ_j w_j e^{i q·r_j}|²/N − ⟨w²⟩) / ⟨w⟩²;   S_ab(q) − 1 = 4πρ ∫ r² (g_ab − 1) sin(qr)/(qr) L(r) dr
symbols: weight: 1, Cromer–Mann f(q) or coherent b
pages.when: Comparing a cell with diffraction data, and neutron contrast with deuterated backbones or rings.
pages.deviation: no q below the cell's first shell 2π/L; no instrument resolution or polarisation factors

pages.title: Free volume and pore sizes
pages.summary: Probe insertion on a grid: a point is free when a probe of the given radius centred there overlaps no van der Waals sphere. Bondi's fractional free volume uses the occupied van der Waals volume; each free point's pore size is the largest atom-free sphere containing it.
pages.equation: FFV = 1 − 1.3 V_w / V;   PSD: d(x) = max { 2R : x ∈ sphere(c, R) free of atoms }
pages.when: Gas permeation, voids in glassy polymers and filled rubbers, pores of frameworks.
pages.deviation: the 1.3 packing factor of Bondi is used as published

pages.title: Mean-square displacement and diffusion
pages.summary: Displacements of atoms and of molecule centres over every time origin, with the drift of the whole system removed. The diffusion coefficient comes from the linear part of the molecule-centre MSD.
pages.equation: D = lim_{t→∞} ⟨|r(t) − r(0)|²⟩ / (6t),   fitted over 20–50 % of the run
pages.when: Small molecules in polymers (curatives, solvents, gases). Check the log–log slope reaches 1 before trusting D.
pages.deviation: no finite-size (Yeh–Hummer) correction

pages.title: Elastic constants by static strain
pages.summary: The minimised cell is strained by ±ε along each of the six components, re-minimised with the pair list frozen, and the stress read from the virial; C_ij are the central differences. Isotropic moduli are Hill averages of the Voigt and Reuss bounds.
pages.equation: C_ij = −(σ_i(+ε_j) − σ_i(−ε_j)) / (2ε),   K_H, G_H = ½(Voigt + Reuss)
pages.when: Glassy polymers and crystals at 0 K. Rubbers above Tg need the fluctuation method or tensile runs.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Elastic constants from stress fluctuations
pages.summary: At finite temperature the elastic constants are the Born term (second strain derivatives of the energy) minus the stress fluctuations, plus the kinetic term, averaged over an NVT run.
pages.equation: C_ijkl = ⟨C^B_ijkl⟩ − (V/k_BT)(⟨σ_ij σ_kl⟩ − ⟨σ_ij⟩⟨σ_kl⟩) + (N k_B T/V)(δ_ik δ_jl + δ_il δ_jk)
pages.when: Finite-temperature constants. For bonded polymers the fluctuation term converges slowly: errors stay at the GPa level over 100 ps, which CAPS reports.
pages.deviation: none

pages.title: Kremer–Grest bead-spring melts
pages.summary: Each chain is a string of beads joined by FENE springs; all beads repel through the WCA potential (Lennard-Jones cut at its minimum and shifted). The model has no chemistry, only connectivity and excluded volume, so it shows the universal physics of polymer melts — entanglements, reptation — at a fraction of the cost. CAPS builds the melt as random walks and writes a LAMMPS deck that pushes the overlaps apart before the real potential starts.
pages.equation: U_FENE = −½ K R₀² ln[1 − (r/R₀)²],   U_WCA = 4ε[(σ/r)¹² − (σ/r)⁶] + ε  for r < 2^{1/6} σ
symbols: bond length of the built walks
bending stiffness, U = k_θ(1 − cos θ)
pages.when: Entanglement and dynamics studies of generic melts and rubbers, and as a fast starting point. Runs in LAMMPS (reduced units); CAPS builds, draws and writes the deck. Model resolution backmaps the beads onto an all-atom structure.
pages.tested: KremerGrest.ChainsBoxAndDeck · the deck run in LAMMPS (P ≈ 5.0 at T = 1, ρσ³ = 0.85)
pages.deviation: the push-off uses LAMMPS pair soft ramped to 60 ε with displacements limited, rather than the force-capped potentials of the paper

pages.title: χ from pair contacts
pages.summary: The Flory–Huggins χ(T) of two components from the energies of their molecules in contact. Each component is one rigid molecule (a solvent, or a repeat unit with its ends capped by hydrogen). Random relative orientations and directions are drawn; the second molecule slides in until the van der Waals surfaces touch, and the pair energy is recorded. The energies are Boltzmann-averaged at each temperature, the coordination numbers come from packing as many molecules as fit around one, and χ(T) is fitted to A + B/T.
pages.equation: ΔE_mix(T) = ½ [Z_AB ⟨E_AB⟩_T + Z_BA ⟨E_BA⟩_T − Z_AA ⟨E_AA⟩_T − Z_BB ⟨E_BB⟩_T],   ⟨E⟩_T = Σ E e^(−E/RT) / Σ e^(−E/RT),   χ(T) = ΔE_mix / RT
symbols: j molecules packed around one i at contact, none overlapping
Bondi radii, solved exactly over every atom pair
GAFF2 with Gasteiger charges in the Studio
pages.when: A predictive screen of solvents and blend partners when no measured solubility parameters exist. In CAPS's check (bench/chi/check_contacts.py) it agrees with known behaviour for 11 of 16 polymer–solvent pairs (Hildebrand: 12 of 16) and fails where single strong contacts dominate: THF, toluene with natural rubber, and polystyrene/PVME (called immiscible; it is miscible). Self-mixing controls resolve χ to about ±0.15.
pages.deviation: rigid molecules with one conformer each; one molecule per lattice site of either kind, with no correction for their different sizes; coordination numbers by random sequential packing

pages.title: Polyhedral template matching
pages.summary: Each particle's nearest neighbours, with the particle itself, are compared with ideal FCC, HCP, BCC, icosahedral and simple-cubic neighbourhoods. Both point sets are centred and scaled to unit mean distance; neighbours are matched to template points from anchor pairs whose angles agree, and the optimal rotation (Horn's quaternion) gives the RMSD. The template with the least RMSD below the cutoff is the particle's structure; its rotation is the lattice orientation, and the deformation left after it gives a shear strain.
pages.equation: RMSD = min_R √(Σ_k |R v̂_k − t̂_π(k)|² / (N + 1)),   F = (Σ x tᵀ)(Σ t tᵀ)⁻¹,   E = ½(FᵀF − I),   ε_shear = √(½ Σ dev(E)²)
symbols: neighbour vectors and template points, centred and scaled
mean neighbour distance over the template's
the nearest-neighbour distance of the local lattice
pages.when: Crystalline fillers and metal particles in a composite: grains, surfaces, stacking faults and local strain; the RMSD table shows where to set the cutoff.
pages.deviation: correspondences from anchor pairs and nearest-point assignment, not the paper's graph-canonical search; the shear strain is relative to the particle's own lattice scale

pages.title: Voronoi and radical tessellation
pages.summary: Each atom's cell is built on its own: a box around it is clipped by the bisecting plane of every neighbour, nearest first, until no farther neighbour can reach the cell (periodic images included). The radical (power) variant moves each plane so that atoms with larger van der Waals radii get larger cells. The cells tile the box exactly; their volumes, faces and the Voronoi index ⟨n3 n4 n5 n6⟩ (faces with 3, 4, 5, 6 edges) follow.
pages.equation: plane between i and j at distance d = (r² + R_i² − R_j²) / (2r) from i (R = 0: Voronoi);   V_i = Σ_faces ⅓ A_f d_f
pages.equation_note: cell-by-cell construction as in Rycroft 2009; radical planes Gellatly & Finney 1982
symbols: distance between the atoms (minimum image or any image)
van der Waals radius (Bondi) in the radical variant
pages.when: Free volume per atom in a polymer (radical), local packing in amorphous metals and fillers; the grid methods remain for a quick look.
pages.deviation: none known; cells of atoms without a periodic cell around them may be open (reported)

pages.title: Wigner–Seitz defect analysis
pages.summary: Every particle is assigned to the reference site nearest to it — the site whose Wigner–Seitz cell holds it. A site without a particle is a vacancy; each particle beyond the first on a site is an interstitial. The reference is a frame of the trajectory (the undamaged lattice) or a file.
pages.equation: site(i) = argmin_k |r_i − R_k| (minimum image),   vacancies = #{k : n_k = 0},   interstitials = Σ_k max(0, n_k − 1)
symbols: a frame of the trajectory or a file
pages.when: Damage in crystalline fillers or substrates: after deformation, irradiation or cutting.
pages.deviation: none known

pages.title: Thiolate ligands on metal particles
pages.summary: Surface atoms of a gold (silver, copper, platinum, palladium) particle are those with fewer neighbours than the bulk. Sulfur sits in three-fold hollows of three mutually neighbouring surface atoms, 2.45 Å from each (on top of an atom where the surface has no hollow), sites at least √3 times the metal's nearest-neighbour distance apart — the √3 × √3 R30° packing of thiolates on Au(111). Each ligand's chain is straightened (all anti) and points out of the surface, rolled about its axis away from the others.
pages.equation: h = √(d_MS² − R²) above the hollow's centre (R: its distance to the three atoms),   d_SS ≥ √3 d_MM
pages.equation_note: packing as reviewed by Love et al. 2005
pages.when: Model a capped nanoparticle to embed or solvate; relax with a force field that has metal–sulfur terms before dynamics (no metal–S bonds are written).
pages.deviation: a geometric placement, not an equilibrated monolayer; adatom (staple) motifs of small clusters are not built

pages.title: OPLS charges from bond increments
pages.summary: OPLS 2005 gives each atom a charge key (an OPLS number chosen by its chemical environment) and each bonded pair of keys an increment that moves charge from one atom to the other. Summing over the bonds gives charges that balance bond by bond, so every molecule keeps its formal charge. OPLS-AA 2024's fixed per-type charges sometimes do not add up where two groups meet (a substituted ring, a benzylic junction); CAPS then uses OPLS 2005's typing and increments for the charges, and OPLS-AA 2024's types for everything else, and says so.
pages.equation: q_i = Σ_j δ_ij over the atoms j bonded to i,   δ_ji = −δ_ij,   δ from the OPLS 2005 table by the pair's keys (its first entry for a pair)
pages.equation_note: OPLS 2005 as in Banks et al. 2005
symbols: the atom's OPLS number from its environment
charge rules in the OPLS 2005 typing file
pages.when: Automatic whenever OPLS-AA 2024's own charges miss the formal charge; by hand with Field › Use OPLS 2005's charges or charges "increments" in recipes and Python.
pages.deviation: charges verified against the reference program's OPLS 2005 on 110 polymers; the combination with OPLS-AA 2024 parameters is CAPS's choice
